translations.translatedText: # Wednesday 22.2.2023 (radio)
Inflation worries Finns. The strike at ports continues. President Niinistö visited Sweden. The anniversary of Russia's attack is remembered in Finland. The weather.
## Finns' financial worries
![Woman with a purse and euro notes.](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_extract,w_1600,h_900,x_0,y_0/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,ar_16:9,dpr_1/f_auto/14-svyle-33059658c7eba87dcc9/1612528826)
Open image viewer
Finns are worried about the effect of inflation on their own economy. Photo: Ismo Pekkarinen / AOP
Inflation, that is, the rise in consumer prices, is currently Finns' biggest financial worry. About 20 percent are very worried about inflation and how it affects their own economy.
The next most common financial worries are the energy crisis and rising housing costs.
The OP Group survey examined Finns' financial worries. About 2,600 people answered the survey in January.
## Dock workers' strike continues

![Signs at the entrance to Vuosaari harbour say AKT strike, closed.](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_extract,w_3984,h_2241,x_0,y_415/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,ar_16:9,dpr_1/f_auto/39-107288563ec6deb351fb/1676439268)
Open image viewer
The dock workers' strike has closed Finland's ports. Photo: Silja Viitala / Yle
Mediation in the dock labour dispute was held today. However, no new compromise proposal was made.
The previous compromise proposal was made on Sunday, but the employees' side, AKT, did not approve it.
The dock workers' strike in Finland's ports has now lasted a week.
The car industry strikes, on the other hand, ended for now last night. For example, the end of the lorry industry strike means that waste is collected again in the usual way.
A new strike may however begin in a week, if no agreement is found in the car industry labour dispute before then.
## Niinistö visited Sweden

![Sauli Niinistö, Ulf Kristersson and Jonas Gahr Støre walk side by side.](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_extract,w_5119,h_2879,x_0,y_0/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,ar_16:9,dpr_1/f_auto/39-107640363f628cfdd81e/1677076739)
Open image viewer
President Sauli Niinistö met Swedish Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson and Norwegian Prime Minister Jonas Gahr Støre. Photo: Markku Ulander / Lehtikuva
President Niinistö has visited Sweden today. There he has met the Prime Ministers of Sweden and Norway.
The topics of discussion were, for example, Finland's and Sweden's Nato membership and support for Ukraine.
After the meeting Niinistö said that Finland still wants to join Nato at the same time as Sweden. Niinistö also said that Finland and Sweden will continue discussions with Turkey together.
Finland and Sweden are now waiting for Turkey and Hungary to confirm their Nato membership.
## A year of war in Ukraine

![Ukrainian flag and a peace sign at an anti-war demonstration in Ukraine.](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_extract,w_3000,h_1679,x_0,y_312/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,ar_16:9,dpr_1/f_auto/39-9201636217e4d597b5d/1645733778)
Open image viewer
Protesters in front of the Russian embassy in Helsinki. Photo: Marja Väänänen / Yle
The day after tomorrow, on Friday, it will be exactly a year since Russia attacked Ukraine.
On the anniversary the Finnish Government shows support for Ukraine by flying the Finnish and Ukrainian flags.

The anniversary is also remembered in many Finnish municipalities. Municipalities can also fly flags and light up buildings in the colours of the Ukrainian flag. In addition, parishes ring church bells across the country and organise events.
In Helsinki a memorial event for the victims of the war will be held at Senate Square. Participants include, for example, President Sauli Niinistö and the Ukrainian Ambassador Olga Dibrova.
## Thursday's weather
![Weather map of Finland.](https://img.img-cdn.yle.fi/crop_fill,w_767,h_431,dpr_1/f_auto/13-3-12689254)
Open image viewer
Photo: Yle
At first it is very cold. At night in the east it may be as much as 30 degrees of frost.
Tomorrow, Thursday, the frost weakens to between zero and 10 degrees of frost.
It snows a little across the whole country. Between three and seven centimetres of new snow will come.
Driving conditions are poor.
